items.title: Venda homeland
items.text: Venda was a bantustan in Northern South Africa, now part of Limpopo province, founded as a homeland for the venda people. It was declared self-governing on February 1, 1973 and declared independent on September 13, 1979, though that independence was never recognised internationally. It was re-absorbed into South Africa on April 27, 1994.

items.title: Geography
items.text: The capital was Thohoyandou, moved there from Sibasa at independence in 1979. Total land area was 6807 square kilometres with a stated 1991 population of 558,797. It bordered Zimbabwe (separated by Madimbo corridor) and Mozambique (separated by Kruger National Park).

items.title: Leadership
items.text: The first President was Patrick Mphephu, who was also a chief of the Venda people. His successor Frank Ravele (overthrown in 1990), after which the territory was ruled by the Council of National Unity.

items.title: Education
items.text: The University of Venda (established in 1982) was set up as an institution of higher learning for vha-Venda people.

items.title: Wildlife and landscape
items.text: Venda is divided into small areas such as Mukhase, where clean water runs off the mountains. Wildlife in the region includes elephants, lions, springbok.

items.title: Language
items.text: Tshivenda is one of the twelve official languages of South Africa and is spoken mainly in northern Limpopo. Its writing system uses letters carrying a mark underneath, such as the d, l, n, t and v forms, which change the sound. This bot matches words with or without those marks so spelling variations still find the right entry.
